newsitem.title: USA: Ariz. utilities say restructure plan needs work.
newsitem.headline: Ariz. utilities say restructure plan needs work.

text.p: More work is needed on several aspects of a plan by the Arizona Corporation Commission (ACC) to restructure the state's electricity industry, Arizona's two large investor-owned utilities said in recent filings.

Pinnacle West's Arizona Public Service Co (APS) and Tucson Electric Power Co asked the commission to reconsider a plan approved last month to open the state's electricity industry to competition over a four-year period beginning in 1999, according to ACC spokesman John Poston.
"We think there are some issues that need to be resolved before competition can begin," said Sally Stewart, a spokeswoman for APS in Phoenix.
Those issues include utilities' stranded costs and reciprocity between both in-state power suppliers and out-of-state competitors, she said.
APS also said the commission's plan is shaky on legal grounds since it does not meet constitutional due process.
The commission has until January 30 to comment on the reconsideration requests, but is not required to do so.
"If the commission decides to let the deadline expire without comment, the companies are free to take it to court," said ACC's Poston.
